guard: the operator-global seed-store payload write announces its path, and only on a real materialization
why: TWO MUTATIONS, ONE PER HALF OF THE PROPERTY, because the announce has a shape and not just a
presence: it must fire when bytes are written and stay quiet when nothing is written. A cell
that only proves the line appears would be held by an announce on every boot, which is the
noise this change is careful not to add, and a cell that only proves the quiet path would be
held by no announce at all.
M1 deletes the announce, which is the defect #593 reports restored exactly: the machine-wide
store write happens and nothing in the output names a path outside the current directory.
M2 does not delete anything. It moves the same announce onto the idempotent reuse path, so the
line appears on a boot that copied no bytes. That is the failure the second cell exists for and
it cannot be caught by M1, since M1 leaves the reuse path exactly as it is.
ORDER, because the suite is fail-fast and a red on the wrong leg is not a kill of the assertion
named. The announce cell runs on the FIRST boot and the quiet cell on the SECOND, so M1 reddens
the earlier of the two and M2 leaves the first boot untouched and reddens only the later one.
Each mutation's named assertion is the first assertion its mutation can reach.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE. It grades the announce, not the isolation. Nothing here shows that
XDG_CONFIG_HOME actually relocates the store: that is existing behaviour this change documents
rather than adds, and remedy 3 of the issue (what `up` should DO when its packages differ from
the published ones at that generation key) is the design question the issue itself declines to
answer and this change does not touch.

mutations.name: the machine-wide store write is silent again (the announce is deleted)
mutations.find:
provenance.wrote(`operator-global seed store payload (${name})`, dest);
  return dest;
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: provenance: the machine-wide seed-store write is announced with its path (not silent)
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: provenance: the machine-wide seed-store write is announced with its path (not silent)

mutations.name: the announce tracks boots rather than writes (the idempotent reuse path announces too)
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: provenance: the idempotent no-op boot announces no seed-store write (announce tracks writes, not boots)
